events.text: A sudden storm, a single pavilion, and a stranger already in it. {npc} offers you half the bench and half a steamed bun and talks about the rain as if it were an old friend.

effects.log: The rain stops at dusk. Neither of you notices for an hour.
A good bun. You think about the stranger more than the bun, which is saying something.

events.text: {npc} turns up at the same pavilion every time it rains. So do you, it turns out. This time {he} has brought two umbrellas and is holding only one of them.

effects.log: Neither of you mentions the second umbrella. You walk the long way home.
{He} laughs at you, a little sadly. The rain is very loud.

events.text: A spring with too little rain. {npc} waits at the pavilion anyway, in the sun, and when you arrive {he} says {he} has run out of excuses.

effects.log: A wedding in the pavilion, in the rain, because you waited for it. Everyone gets wet. Nobody minds.
{He} nods, and still waits at the pavilion when it rains, for a while.

events.text: The tournament pairs you with {npc} in the first round. {He} fights like a storm and insults your footwork the whole time. You lose. {He} buys you tea afterwards, still insulting it.

effects.log: 'Every year,' {he} says. 'Until one of us gets it right.'
{He} laughs so hard {he} spills the drink.

events.text: The rematch. You win this time, and {npc} sits in the dust looking up at you with an expression you have not seen on a defeated face before.

effects.log: Neither of you lets go for a moment too long. The crowd notices before you do.
{He} watches you go. The next rematch, {he} wins, and does not look pleased about it.

events.text: Yet another rematch. {npc} stops in the middle of the bout, lowers {his} sword, and says {he} would rather spend the rest of the years fighting beside you than against you.

effects.log: You marry in the arena, under the same banners, and the tournament officials argue for a week about who won.

ok.log: {He} smiles and raises {his} sword again. Some loves are better at sword's length.

fail.log: {He} beats you back across the sand, laughing, and does not ask again. The years go on, side by side and at sword's length.

events.text: You are carried into a medicine hall half-dead after a fight, and {npc}, the youngest healer, stitches you up while telling you exactly how stupid you were.

effects.log: 'Do not come back,' {he} says. You come back the next week with a very small cut.

choices.text: Argue that you were not stupid

effects.log: {He} pulls the next stitch tighter. You both enjoy the argument.

events.text: A plague in the next town and {npc} is going. The hall says it is too dangerous. {He} asks you to carry the medicine chest, since you are so good at getting hurt.

mem.note: carried the chest into the plague

effects.log: A month of plague. {He} sleeps on your shoulder in the wagon home.
{He} goes anyway. You worry the whole month.

events.text: {npc} stitches your newest wound, very slowly, and then does not let go of your hand. 'I am tired,' {he} says, 'of only seeing you when you are bleeding.'

effects.log: You marry. You come home bleeding anyway, often. {He} stitches you up every time, and complains, and you both like it.
{He} finishes the stitch in silence. That is the honest answer, and it hurts you both.

events.text: Someone picks your pocket in the market. You catch {npc} by the wrist, and {he} grins and puts back your purse, plus a coin {he} stole from someone else, as an apology.

effects.log: {He} winks and vanishes into the crowd. Your purse is a little heavier.
{He} eats like a wolf and tells you the history of every merchant in the market, most of it true.

events.text: {npc} has been caught by the constables and faces ten years in the magistrate's cells. {He} sees you in the crowd and does not ask for anything.

effects.log: {He} walks out free and walks straight to you.

ok.log: Over the roof and out of the city by dawn, laughing.

fail.log: A guard sees the rope. You and {him} both spend the night behind the same bars, which is a story of its own.

events.text: {npc} has gone straight. {He} has a stall in the market, mends locks, and has not stolen anything in a year, except, {he} says, your attention.

effects.log: A wedding in the market. Half the guests are reformed thieves. Nobody's purse goes missing, which everyone agrees is a miracle.
{He} sells you the lock, smiling. It is a very good lock. You never forget the smile.

events.text: A letter floats down the river in a sealed bottle. It is from {npc}, who lives upstream, and is a poem about loneliness that is also very funny.

effects.log: You put your reply in a bottle and throw it upstream, which does not work. You walk it up instead.
You read it so often the ink fades. Then a second bottle comes.

events.text: A hundred letters, back and forth. {npc} writes that {he} is coming down the river, and that you should meet {him} at the bridge, and that {he} is afraid you will not like {his} face.

effects.log: You know {him} at once, by the way {he} stands. You like {his} face very much.

choices.text: Write that you are afraid too

effects.log: {He} writes back that this is the bravest letter yet. The meeting waits another year.

events.text: {npc} puts a last letter in your hand, sealed, and asks you to open it in front of {him}. It has one line on it.

effects.log: You marry on the bridge between your two villages. Both villages throw letters into the river, for luck.
You write a long answer that does not say yes or no. {He} reads it many times.

events.text: {npc} guards the gate of the sect you are visiting and refuses to let you in without a token. You argue for an hour. {He} enjoys every minute and still does not let you in.

effects.log: On the ninth day {he} lets you in. On the tenth you do not go in, you just talk at the gate.

ok.log: {He} is waiting on the other side, arms folded, trying very hard not to smile.

fail.log: You make it halfway up and the wall makes the rest of the decision. {He} catches you on the way down, and lets you think it was an accident.

events.text: Raiders hit the sect at night and {npc} is alone at the gate when they come. You are there because you always are.

ok.log: The raiders break on the two of you. The sect master finds you at dawn, back to back, still standing.

fail.log: There are too many. You go down at the gate with {him} beside you, and the sect arrives just in time to find you both breathing.

effects.log: You bring the whole sect down on the raiders. {He} says thank you, and that you could have stayed.

events.text: {npc} has been offered a post as an inner disciple, far from the gate. {He} asks whether there is a reason to stay.

effects.log: You marry at the gate, of course. {He} takes the inner post anyway, and you go with {him}, and nobody needs a token.
{He} goes. The new gate guard is very strict and nothing like {him}.
